name: Hydrogen-sponge spacecraft hull
subtitle: a spacecraft wall that is shield and fuel

effects.effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
radiation ionizes what it passes through

effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
how: On the way to Mars, cosmic rays give a crew a serious cancer risk, and the best shield per kilogram is hydrogen, whose light nuclei stop fast particles without shattering into showers of secondary radiation. The hull walls are packed with crystal sponges that hold hydrogen gas densely, wrapping the crew in a shield for the long cruise; near arrival the same hydrogen is drawn off as landing fuel, once the worst of the trip is over.
obstacle: The sponges hold enough hydrogen only near minus 200 °C, so the walls still need constant, heavy cooling.
why: Water walls proposed as dual-use shields; nobody has built a hydrogen-sponge hull.
real: Simulation studies (2015, 2025) and an ESA project propose hydrogen-loaded MOFs as spacecraft radiation shielding; no hardware.
